newsitem.title: UK: Promise of new issues boosts London emerging debt.
newsitem.headline: Promise of new issues boosts London emerging debt.

text.p: Strength in US Treasuries carried through into London's emerging debt market, with the promise of new issues in Latin America and eastern Europe helping to boost prices and sentiment, traders said.

"There's been a little selling of MinFin bonds, but the profit-taking has been more than made up -- prices are back a bit firmer in anticipation of the new Eurobond coming out," one Russian debt trader said.
Another said talk that Brazil was also planning a global bond, with a $750 million five or 10-year issue seen possibly as soon as next week, was helping prices there.
Brazil C bonds were quoted up 1/4 at 71-3/4 at 1145 GMT. Issues three to six of Russia's Taiga or MinFin bonds all firmed, with the MinFin 6 up 5/8 at 10-1/8.
The Russian debt trader said firmness in Russia's T-bill or GKO market was also underpinning the MinFins' rise, while dollar Vnesh paper strengthened 1/2 to 68-3/4.
"The FOMC started this going, and that was coupled with the Yeltsin operation with its success now felt to be assured," he said.
"The operation will definitely happen, the market is pleased to have more definite information and is reassured by having a US surgeon in attendance," he added.
Earlier this week the US Federal Reserve decided not to raise interest rates, and emerging debt prices breathed a sigh of relief.

Russia's plans to launch a eurobond, talk of another from the City of Moscow, and growing expectations of an investment grade rating for Russia in the meantime, also contributed to the buoyant mood, though trading volumes were moderate, the trader added.

Bulgarian paper continued to recover from last week's losses after news that Bulgarian Bradys could be used in the country's speeded-up privatisation process, and progress in meeting reform targets upon which hinges a $115 million IMF tranche.
Bulgarian FLRBS gained 5/8 during the morning, rising to 33-1/4 by 1200 GMT.
Latin American debt prices were a touch firmer too, with Argentine FRBs up 1/4 at 84-3/8.
Mexican Pars were flat at 70-1/2, but Venezuelan DCBs climbed 1/2 to 83-1/4 amid a generally positive market tone. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
